title: Learn More About P&G’s Climate Initiatives and Net Zero Ambition
summary: Climate change action and waste reduction align with P&G's ambition of net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040. Learn about our strategies, partnerships and the role of consumers in our journey.
body_markdown:
## 6. Does P&G use offsets as part of its climate strategy?


Our top priority is to reduce our absolute greenhouse gas emissions. We have accelerated our efforts here and will continue to invest in new solutions to drive reductions further.


We acknowledge that nature is a powerful solution today that can reduce CO2 in the atmosphere. That’s why, for emissions we do not eliminate, we will explore natural or technical solutions to remove an equivalent amount of GHG emissions from the atmosphere. This includes collaborating with environmental NGOs to support projects that protect and restore forests and ecosystems. Learn more about our nature efforts[HERE](https://www.pginvestor.com/esg/environmental/nature/partnerships/default.aspx) .


## 7. What challenges does P&G face in its climate journey?


We realize there’s a need for new technologies to help reduce the impacts of climate change. We view these challenges as opportunities for growth and innovation, and we are committed to learning and adapting as we move forward. P&G is enabling people to reduce their environmental impact at home when they use our products and partnering to scale industry-wide solutions that will accelerate success for all of us – P&G, our consumers, and our industry. Reducing greenhouse gas emissions requires both ingenuity and partnership. In our path to net zero, we are looking toward using technology that exists today to reduce emissions, investing in new solutions and materials innovation, and embracing transformative collaboration.


## 8. How can consumers contribute to P&G’s climate efforts?


Our strategy is focused on innovation that solves everyday problems through irresistible superiority that drives market growth and is more environmentally sustainable. Consumers can play an important role by making small changes in their daily routines, such as using cold water for washing clothes to reduce energy consumption.


Through our long-standing partnership with World Wildlife Fund (WWF), we support efforts that help consumers take simple actions that can add up to a meaningful impact over time. WWF collaborates with brands like Tide and Ariel to promote sustainable habits at home, including washing laundry in cold water, which can help reduce energy use while extending the life of clothing. Together, we aim to help make sustainable choices easier in everyday routines.


## 9. How does P&G measure and track progress toward its climate goals?


P&G tracks progress toward defined climate goals and metrics and reports results through our Citizenship Report and[ESG Investor Portal](https://www.pginvestor.com/esg/environmental/Environmental-Overview/default.aspx) . We use science-based targets to guide our efforts and regularly publish data on key measures, including greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption.


P&G follows the guidelines of the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting Standard. We also provide independent assurance for greenhouse gas emissions data reported through our climate disclosures.


## 10. How can I stay up-to-date with P&G’s climate efforts?


P&G is dedicated to transparency and will share updates on our progress toward net zero through our[ESG Investor portal](https://www.pginvestor.com/esg/environmental/Environmental-Overview/default.aspx) and in our Citizenship Report.


Addressing climate change is complex and requires innovation and collaboration. We’re delivering impact at three levels: reducing our own impact, enabling consumers to reduce their impact and helping industry reduce its environmental impact through scalable solutions.


**Explore our[Climate Transition Action Plan](https://s204.q4cdn.com/332108499/files/doc_downloads/PG_CTAP.pdf) to learn more about P&G’s climate initiatives and our ambition of achieving net zero emissions by 2040.**
